# Blackboard submission

Use this skill only for the CSCI 6032 Homework 2 repository
`https://github.com/enreysen-um/csci6032-hw2-enreysen-um`.
This workflow is intentionally fail-closed. Do not weaken a check to make
submission proceed.

## Permission and privacy rules

- Before any command that reads repository state, explain what it will inspect
  and ask for permission. Do not preapprove shell or browser tools.
- Before opening, focusing, or controlling a Blackboard tab, explain the
  action and ask for permission. A dry run must never open or control
  Blackboard.
- The student must authenticate personally in the browser. Never ask for,
  read, store, type, copy, or expose a password, MFA code, session token,
  cookie, recovery code, or other credential. Never use browser automation to
  bypass authentication.
- Do not request or save personal information beyond the GitHub username
  needed in the archive filename and the repository URL. Do not print
  credentials or browser state.
- Do not commit screenshots, receipts, browser data, personal information, or
  the generated archive to the public repository.

## 1. Confirm the repository

Ask permission to inspect the current working directory and repository root.
Stop unless the resolved root is the expected repository and the remote is the
expected GitHub repository. Do not operate on a similarly named directory.

Expected identity:

```text
repository: enreysen-um/csci6032-hw2-enreysen-um
remote URL: https://github.com/enreysen-um/csci6032-hw2-enreysen-um.git
```

Treat an SSH URL as acceptable only if it resolves exactly to that repository;
show the normalized repository identity, not private configuration.

## 2. Preflight

Ask permission to run the complete read-only preflight. Check and display:

1. The current branch name.
2. `git status --short --branch`; stop if any tracked, staged, or untracked
   change is present. Ignored files are not enough to declare a dirty tree if
   they could be included in the archive, so inspect archive inputs too.
3. Recent commits, including the `HEAD` commit hash and subject.
4. The configured remote URL, which must identify the expected repository.
5. Required committed files:
   - `README.md`
   - `CSCI6032_hw2.ipynb`
   - `src/text_stats.py`
   - `tests/test_text_stats.py`
   - `sample.txt`
   - `.gitignore`

Also inspect the candidate archive file list for credentials, private data,
browser artifacts, caches, generated bytecode, editor state, `.git`, and files
outside the homework. Stop if any unresolved secret or private data is
apparent, including `.env`, key/certificate files, tokens, cookies, password
files, browser profiles, screenshots, receipts, or files containing credential
material. Do not open suspicious files to investigate their contents; report
the path and ask the student to remove or resolve it.

## 3. Confirm the reviewed branch is pushed

After the student reviews the preflight output, ask permission to perform the
read-only synchronization check. Confirm that `HEAD` is pushed to the
configured expected remote and that the remote-tracking branch contains the
same commit. If the branch has no upstream, is ahead of its upstream, or the
remote cannot be verified, stop and instruct the student to push it
personally. Never push without a separate explicit request and confirmation.

## 4. Build the archive from committed `HEAD`

Ask for the student’s GitHub username if it is not already known from the
student, or obtain only the account login through an already authenticated,
user-approved GitHub CLI query. Do not ask for GitHub credentials. Validate the
username as a GitHub login and use exactly:

```text
csci6032-hw2-<github-username>.tar.gz
```

Ask permission to create the archive in a temporary location outside the
repository, using only files reachable from the reviewed committed `HEAD`
(for example, `git archive --format=tar.gz --output=<temporary archive> HEAD`).
Never archive the working directory directly. Exclude `.git`, credentials,
private data, caches, generated bytecode, browser artifacts, screenshots,
receipts, the temporary archive itself, and unrelated files. If a prohibited
path is tracked by `HEAD`, stop rather than silently modifying or omitting the
committed homework; report it for student resolution.

## 5. Inspect the exact submission package

List the archive contents from the generated archive and verify that the
required notebook is present exactly once and that no prohibited path is
present. Show the student, without exposing sensitive content:

- the exact notebook path;
- the exact archive path and byte size;
- the exact repository URL;
- the exact submission text to paste.

Use concise submission text such as:

```text
CSCI 6032 Homework 2 submission.
Notebook: CSCI6032_hw2.ipynb
Repository: https://github.com/enreysen-um/csci6032-hw2-enreysen-um
Archive: csci6032-hw2-<github-username>.tar.gz
```

Do not upload or commit the archive until the student has reviewed these
details.

## 6. Dry run

Support a `dry-run` request. In dry-run mode, perform every possible local
check above, including repository identity, clean status, required files,
secret/private-data screening, archive creation in a temporary location,
archive listing, exact submission text, and pushed-branch verification.
Report that no Blackboard tab was opened, no files were staged in Blackboard,
and no submission was made. Remove the temporary archive after reporting its
validated contents, unless the student explicitly requests a separately
approved local artifact.

## 7. Blackboard staging

Only after the dry run or equivalent checks pass, ask separately for permission
to open or control Blackboard. Navigate only to the CSCI 6032 Homework 2
submission page. Do not search unrelated courses, assignments, accounts, or
messages.

The student must authenticate in the visible browser session personally.
Pause for authentication and never handle credentials. After authentication,
stage only the required archive, the notebook if the page requires a separate
notebook upload, and the repository URL/submission text. Do not submit yet.
If the page is not clearly this homework’s submission page, stop immediately.

## 8. Final irreversible confirmation

Before clicking the final Submit/Turn In action, stop and display exactly what
will be submitted: the destination page title/course/assignment, filenames
and sizes, notebook path, repository URL, and submission text. Explain that
the next action is irreversible or may trigger grading. Ask for a fresh,
explicit confirmation at this point. A prior general approval, approval to
open Blackboard, or approval to stage files is not sufficient.

If confirmation is not explicit, do not submit.

## 9. Complete and verify

Only after the immediate confirmation, perform the final submission. Verify
the resulting confirmation page, submission status, timestamp, or receipt
visible in Blackboard. Report the result and any receipt identifier without
copying credentials, cookies, screenshots, or personal data into the
repository. Do not commit or upload Blackboard screenshots, receipts,
browser data, or personal information to GitHub.
